candidate.entry_event: entry-time observation of sustained basis dislocation (futures basis divergence) accompanied by rising open_interest and skewed funding direction in funding
candidate.exit_logic: maintain position until basis mean-reverts or open_interest and funding direction weaken, or until unwind liquidity stress appears; time-stop set to typical contract mean-reversion horizon (multi-day) matching institutional basis unwind cycles
candidate.falsification: prospective kill test: require N consecutive qualification events (e.g., 10) where basis reversion magnitude over natural multi-day horizon fails to exceed 2x verified round-trip cost before funding and OI normalize
candidate.invalidation: if basis/basis-driving speculative demand no longer predicts persistent premium decompression when conditioned on OI/funding signals, the arbitrage/unwind mechanism collapses
candidate.mechanism: persistent speculative-imposed basis dislocations are corrected by arbitrageurs or forced deleveraging; the payer is the speculative demand and funding-imposed costs; profits accrue by positioning to capture the unwind over days
candidate.payer: speculative demand and leveraged futures holders
candidate.regime_owner: only trade when basis dislocation is supported by rising OI and consistent asymmetric funding; avoid calm or structurally hedged regimes
candidate.time_stop_rationale: time-stop matches the typical unwind/mean-reversion timeframe for basis adjustments driven by funding and OI dynamics, avoiding premature exits
candidate.turnover_cost_budget: multi-day basis moves can be large relative to verified round-trip cost, enabling per-trade expected move to exceed transaction costs if entries require OI+funding confirmation
candidate.why_distinct: unlike simple funding-threshold carry bets, this architecture ties entry to joint OI and basis dynamics, owning the unwind mechanism rather than reacting to funding alone
